brief_extract: Later, in the Middle Ages, it is known that rents were sometimes paid in eggs. brief_context: Where specific egg-eating customs were practiced.
article_title: Advertisement: British Egg Information Service - The history of Eggs
brief_extract: The egg, representing fertility, conveyed superstition and fear which influenced eating customs. This was demonstrated in the Philippines and Pacific Islands where it was considered 'safer' to eat eggs inside which a chicken was already forming: or alternatively among some African tribes which demanded that 'life' inside the egg should be killed by cooking or rotting. Problems were created in other places such as India where distrust of the hen's 'dirty' feeding habits forced hungry natives to refuse eggs and thereby, a valuable source of nourishment.

brief_context: Renowned for the art of decorating eggs.
article_title: Advertisement: British Egg Information Service - The history of Eggs
brief_extract: The tradition of dying and decorating eggs is thousands of years old, and has given some outstandingly beautiful examples of artistry to posterity. The Ukraine is renowned for this art which has, since around 3000 B.C., represented religious associations and revealed deep, human feelings. Ancient Egyptians, Greeks and Romans dyed eggs, and Persians ornamented eggs to exchange with friends as a renewal of all things.

brief_context: Location where WAC discussed standards for household linen.
article_title: The Women's Advisory Committee (WAC) of the British Standards Institution (BSI)
brief_extract: The WAC's influence on manufacturers and retailers makes itself most felt through the work of its representatives on BSI technical committees, but from time to time meetings are arranged for special purposes. For example, it has organised discussions with manufacturers, retailers and other interested parties on such subjects as school uniforms and children's and women's shoes and it has sent representatives to Belfast to discuss with the Irish Linen Industry the possibility of standards for household linen. The WAC is very conscious of the importance of publicity and it does its best to keep journalists and broadcasters in touch with its work.

article_title: The Women's Advisory Committee (WAC) of the British Standards Institution (BSI)
brief_extract:
New publicity material is produced whenever funds permit. Increasing attention is being paid to co-operation with schools and colleges and the Education Sub-Committee on which a number of teachers, inspectors and other educationists are represented is currently planning a new series of teaching aids as well as commissioning a film about the consumer work of BSI which is being made by the film unit of Harrow College of Technology and Art. Progress and Achievements
With its coming of age the WAC knows it will be asked to list its achievements over the years and it is tempting to highlight a few outstanding successes at the expense of slow but steady and unspectacular progress in other directions.

HARROGATE, which members of the EAW will be visiting for their conference this year, is a town with four centuries of practice at hospitality behind it.

location_standardised: Edinburgh, City of Edinburgh, Scotland, United Kingdom
brief_context: Used as a geographic reference point for Harrogate's location.
brief_extract: After all, Harrogate was receiving flocks of seasonal visitors long before it occurred to any-one to visit a seaside resort. Placed geographic-ally half-way between Edinburgh and London and half-way between the west coast of Lancashire and the east coast of Yorkshire, Harrogate is about as inland as you can get and might have developed as no more than a pleasant farming area on the fringe of the West Riding had it not been discovered that beneath its clay soil (excellent for roses) there bubbled a con-siderable number of springs of various mineral and medicinal waters. The doctors of the 17th century were great ones for advocating nature cures and compared with some of their prescriptions, Harrogate's iron, chalybeate, or sulphur water must have seemed like ambrosia.

brief_context: A vast 200-acre public common in Harrogate.
brief_extract: In that period, much of the town's economy was orientated towards the entertainment of visitors who found in Harrogate the large and luxurious hotels, the bathing establishments and the concert halls and parks they needed. Above all, they found that with admirable foresight, the town's pioneers had secured as a public common for ever a vast horseshoe of 200 acres of grassland, known as The Stray, round and alongside which the town's buildings developed. Long since fringed with trees, this Stray is Harrogate's most jealously guarded possession.

brief_context: Beautiful countryside accessible from Harrogate.
brief_extract: Window shopping in the town centre is a special delight whatever one's interests may be—dresses, furs, jewellery, silver, antiques, or modern furnishings. Conference visitors who find themselves with a little time to spare will find that Harrogate is not only a beautiful town in itself but also the gateway to a lovely countryside which ranges from rural charm to the wild splendours of the Yorkshire Dales, and there are aspects of history everywhere. It takes hardly an hour in a car to reach Whernside, the peak where the River Nidd has its source; and the ancient town of Knares- borough, with its romantic castle overlooking the last gorge of the Nidd before it flows into the plain of York, is not four miles away.

There is a choice of stately homes: Rudding Park, literally on Harrogate's doorstep, built in the reign of William IV and set in a Capability Brown park; Harewood House, nine miles away, a treasure-house of Chippendale masterpieces; Newby Hall, near Ripon, with its Gobelin tapestries, and, farther afield, Bramham Park's Versailles style gardens and Castle Howard, a monument to Vanbrugh's genius. And, of course, there is an ever wonderful Fountain Abbey at Studley, near Ripon, which ancient city has its own treasures, among them a fine cathedral, and again farther afield but easily reached the restored glories of York Minster and the abbeys of Byland, Jervaulx and Coverham.

article_title: Air Conditioning Prospects in Great Britain
brief_extract:
Air Conditioning Prospects
in Great Britain
by ROBERT POLLARD, CENG, MIEE, The Electricity Council

AIR conditioning is essential to comfortable living in countries like the United States because without it the very high summer temperatures make indoor living conditions quite intolerable. In Britain, many still consider it to be an expensive luxury, made unnecessary by the ‘temperate’ British climate; but in view of the much higher humidity conditions which exist in this country it is just as essential here.

location_standardised: Birmingham, West Midlands, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Location where temperature records were kept during July 1967.
article_title: Air Conditioning Prospects in Great Britain
brief_extract: Most people consider the summer of 1967 as a hot summer. Yet records kept in Birmingham, for example, showed that during July the temperature rose above 21°C (70°F) on only five days, and only on one of those days did it rise above 24°C (76°F). It was the solar radiation, internal heat gains combined with high humidity conditions, averaging 70 per cent relative humidity in London during the summer and higher in the north, which caused discomfort and not outside temperature.

Lady De La Warr (centre) with Miss George and Mr Claude Simmons, Chairman of the Food Freezer Committee at the launching of the EAW freezer display

FOOD freezers are rapidly becoming popular as more and more people realise what an asset they can be in the home, saving time, cutting food bills and making catering so much simpler. brief_extract:

VISIT TO SOUTH OF SCOTLAND ELECTRICITY BOARD, HAMILTON
by MRS E. BROOKMAN, East Kilbride Branch. Before the tour the following explanation of the basic figures was given:
Electricity is generated at the Generating Station to high voltage — 275,000 volts, supplied to the Grid Sub-stations at 33,000 volts, transformed there to 11,000 volts, then to small sub-stations where it is transformed down to 415-240 volts, the latter being that for domestic use.

location_standardised: London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Location of National Control for the electricity grid.
article_title: VISIT TO SOUTH OF SCOTLAND ELECTRICITY BOARD, HAMILTON
brief_extract: The Control Room was first visited. There are three systems of control — National Control in London where generation over the whole country is controlled and forward assessments made of con- sumers’ requirements; Group Control of which the Scottish centre is Kirkintilloch, and Area Control under which category Hamilton comes. From the centre in Hamilton the Control Engineer is capable of selecting and controlling 33 circuit breakers as far north as Stirling and as far south as Dumfries and Galloway.

brief_context: Country excluded from mustard exports.
article_title: VISIT TO RECKITT & COLMANS, CARROW WORKS, NORWICH
brief_extract: WAYTE, Magazine Secretary, Gt Yarmouth Afternoon Branch. Reckitt & Colmans (Food Division) which incor- porates the only mustard factory in the world covers 57 acres and exports mustard to every country in the world except Russia and the Communist Bloc. Mustard was the firm’s original product.

brief_context: Export destination for mustard seed husks.
article_title: VISIT TO RECKITT & COLMANS, CARROW WORKS, NORWICH
brief_extract: There are two kinds of mustard seed, brown and white, which are processed, refined and blended together to produce the table mustard. The seed husks are converted into many by-products some of which are exported to the USA. The factory takes the whole output of certain tin mines in Wales and, at one time, had its own silk worms for making the fine silk screens through which the mustard is sifted, but now the silk is imported from abroad.

brief_context: Location of tin mines supplying the factory.
article_title: VISIT TO RECKITT & COLMANS, CARROW WORKS, NORWICH
brief_extract: The seed husks are converted into many by-products some of which are exported to the USA. The factory takes the whole output of certain tin mines in Wales and, at one time, had its own silk worms for making the fine silk screens through which the mustard is sifted, but now the silk is imported from abroad. The tour began with an inspection of the raw materials, tinplate and plastic used for containers, and the all-electric machines for making the bottles for Robinsons fruit drinks and Jif lemons, a fas- cinating process resulting in an army of these passing along on conveyor belts to the filling and capping machines.

brief_extract: In her Caroline Haslett Memorial Trust Lecture on Nation Building and the African Woman Dr Letitia Obeng stressed that the acquisition of the relevant 'know-how' through formal education was a necessity for women to play their full part. As she stated, without it even a queen-mother in Ghana with all her traditional power, her sophistication and business astuteness could not participate effectively in policy-making decisions. Know-how related to the circumstances of the 1970s is a basic requirement of management.

EAW BRANCH SUPPLEMENT

The 'Know-how'
that matters

'KNOW-HOW' has always been important in most spheres of activity but in today's technical society it has tended to replace traditional knowledge and skills. While it has long been recognised as essential in industry it is now part and parcel of commercial life and women have come to realise that they must have 'know-how' of the right kind to succeed in their professional careers and to run their homes to best advantage.

brief_extract:
Bread Varieties
Bread varies throughout the country and many regions have their specialities and particular names. Scottish bread has a slightly salty flavour. Because of this higher salt content, the dough needs longer rising than for other bread.

brief_extract: The baked bread has good keeping qualities. The main loaf of Scotland is batch or square bread—these white loaves are baked in pairs. The pan or sandwich loaf, also white, is popular too.

article_title: A British Woman at Harvard Business School
brief_extract:
A British Woman at Harvard Business School
by JEAN GOMM, bursary holder of the Caroline Haslett Memorial Trust

“WHAT’S a nice girl like you doing in a place like this?” a question frequently asked by both fellow students and companies who come to interview on the campus of Harvard Business School in America. I find that it does seem strange to many and requires explanation that a 25-year-old English girl should be studying for a Master’s Degree in Business Administration at the world’s No 1 Management School.

brief_context: Country where the author is studying.
article_title: A British Woman at Harvard Business School
brief_extract:
A British Woman at Harvard Business School
by JEAN GOMM, bursary holder of the Caroline Haslett Memorial Trust

“WHAT’S a nice girl like you doing in a place like this?” a question frequently asked by both fellow students and companies who come to interview on the campus of Harvard Business School in America. I find that it does seem strange to many and requires explanation that a 25-year-old English girl should be studying for a Master’s Degree in Business Administration at the world’s No 1 Management School.

brief_context: The author's home country.
article_title: A British Woman at Harvard Business School
brief_extract: Just 5% of the school’s students are women and I am one of the first two English girls ever to attend the MBA course. I arrived at Harvard via a career in personnel management and completed the first year of the MBA course at Cranfield Management School in England, gained an MBA from there and then was accepted by Harvard, directly into the second year of their two year Master’s programme, to study International Business. The transition from Cranfield Management School with about 70 students to Harvard with 1,500 was a strange one.

brief_context: The school where the author completed her first MBA year.

The transition from Cranfield Management School with about 70 students to Harvard with 1,500 was a strange one.

location_standardised: Harvard University, Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States
brief_context: The university where the author is studying.
brief_extract: And if I need help, I have available some of the best authorities in the world for guidance. My time at Harvard comes to an end in June when I graduate. I am presently in the throes of deciding what I want to do as a career.

location_standardised: New York, New York, United States
brief_context: Location of an agency the author is working for.
brief_extract: The stimulating atmosphere encourages one to attempt more and more, and to test one's abilities. Since my arrival here in September, I have done a consultancy project for a super-market chain, written articles for several news-papers and magazines, started to set up an organisation for other women considering Business School training, am researching the field of Equal Opportunity Laws, researching how small American companies make investment decisions, and working on a proposed new division of a small New York agency. I find, often to my surprise, that the more I try, the more I find I can do.

brief_context: The country the author hopes to return to.
brief_extract: I am looking mainly at the field of International Business and Consultancy, preferably on an international basis. My hope is to return to England, but as I have borrowed a considerable amount of money to finance my studies, I may be forced to stay in America for the next year or so. The British salary and taxation system do not facilitate loan repayment.

brief_extract:
Special Events at EAW Branches

VISIT TO RONSON ELECTRICS, CRAMLINGTON
by MRS B. STORRAR, Magazine Secretary, Middlesbrough Branch

Members enjoyed a well conducted and exhaustive visit to this all-electric bright modern factory on a new trading estate. Only electrical equipment is produced at this factory and all the jigs, machines, furnaces, testing equipment, even soldering irons, and assembly lines are electrically operated.

brief_context: Export destination for the hair-dryers produced at Ronson.
brief_extract: The Ronson Escort 2000 which is the luxury dryer with carrying strap, hood and variable heat controls packed in a vanity case complete with hot air comb and brush; the Ronson Rapide; and the Dual Volt Rio which is a small compact dryer much favoured for travelling and by teenagers. All the dryers being assembled at the time of the visit were for export to Scandinavia, hence the dual voltage, and members were interested to learn that a large proportion of the export quota goes to Africa. Most of the operatives were very young and there is a training school for 15-year-old school-leavers.

brief_extract:
The New Chairman

After the Annual General Meeting at Harrogate this year MRS JOAN COOK took over as Chairman of the National Executive Committee, and the following discussion with MISS MARY GEORGE, the Director, reveals some of Mrs Cook's background in the EAW and her hopes for its future. Mrs Cook (left) and Miss George

Miss George.

location_standardised: London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Branch of the EAW where Mrs Cook began her career.
brief_extract: My father had been an invalid and at home we always had to get an electrician in to deal with such things as plugs and fuses. I often used to say I wished I could do these jobs and then some years later in 1953 my mother saw a notice in the old Star newspaper which described an electrical course for the public run by the London Branch of the Electrical Association for Women. She sent this to me and said 'This is just the thing for you' and I enrolled and presented myself on the appointed day.

brief_context: County where Mrs Joan Cook resides in a village.
brief_extract: Mrs Cook. As you know I live in a village in Kent and I like to take a real part in all that is going on. I was on the Parish Council for a time.

location_standardised: London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Council of which Mrs Cook is a member.
brief_extract: Miss George. Another claim on your time is membership of the London Electricity Consultative Council. How do you assess the value of this work?

location_standardised: London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Acronym for London Electricity Board mentioned regarding meter cards.
brief_extract: People often just do not understand their electricity bills and cannot believe that they have used the amount of electricity which is reflected in the bill. They are also worried by estimated accounts and I am very pleased that in some districts of the LEB self-reading meter cards are being re-introduced. Miss George.

location_standardised: London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Referring to the London Electricity Board.
brief_extract: Yes, it is a very big problem and there are still far too many people who have to wait too long for such things as a handle, and the right handle, to be put on a cooker. The London Board, along with all the other Boards, is trying to get more rationalisation of stocks in co-operation with the manufacturers and I think the position is beginning to improve. Miss George.

brief_context: Mentioned regarding the formation of the Exeter Young Electrics branch.
brief_extract: They like to form their own groups. I think, too, that it is essential to have some special attraction for young people, and one of the newest members of the National Executive Committee who was associated with the formation of the Exeter Young Electrics told me that this branch developed out of a Brides' Course. Miss George.

brief_context: The author mentioned touring in a caravan in Scotland.
brief_extract:
KINLOCH, DFH, CENG, MIEE
Assistant Chief Engineer, National Inspection Council for Electrical Installation Contracting
ONCE again the holiday season has passed and I expect that you are looking back on the pleasures of summer as well as looking forward with varying feelings to the coming winter. For myself, the memories are of touring in my caravan in Scotland when my wife and I revert to the simple life with a carpet area of only 3 square metres to be cleaned and meals cooked by means of two gas rings and a grill. We become so accustomed to living in a small space that it seems strange when we return home and, even after several days, I sometimes try to operate a non-existent foot pump to obtain water at the kitchen sink!

brief_context: One of the regions where the scholarship offer is notified.
article_title: Chosen Girls: Scholarship Holders of the Caroline Haslett Memorial Trust
brief_extract: Many of them have real leadership potential which augurs well for the contribution which they will be qualified to make both to technological advancement and to the community. One of the many questions people ask the Trust is 'How do you manage to select just one or two scholars each year from a large number of candidates?' What happens is that first of all the offer of a university scholarship is notified each year to all girls' schools and mixed schools in Britain through the Joint Committee of the Four Secondary Associations in England and Wales and through the Directors of Education in Scotland. Application forms are obtainable from the Trust and these candidates have to give details of their scholastic careers to date, the reasons for choosing a technological career, and an account of their other interests and hobbies.

location_standardised: Dollis Hill, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Location of the Post Office Research Station visited by members.
brief_extract:
The Telephone Today and Tomorrow
THE telephone has long been a vital part of everyday life but few of us realise the extent of the present system and the immense amount of fascinating research which is being undertaken both for the immediate and the long-term future. During a visit to the Post Office Research Station at Dollis Hill in North West London members of London Branch of the EAW gained an insight into the ways in which scientists, several of them women, were working on such subjects as the more easily understood human factors, and the extremely complicated subjects of submarine cable systems, computer-aided circuit design and new materials for transmission. The ergonomic studies regarding the design of handsets, including push-button units, and the location of sets to suit people of varying heights were of immediate interest.

brief_context: Radar monitors ships in the channel near Dover.
article_title: VISIT TO TRINITY HOUSE PILOT STATION, FOLKESTONE
brief_extract:
BOORMAN, Magazine Secretary, Folkestone Branch

When visiting Trinity House members were made fully aware of the value of electricity to those at sea. In the observation room are two radar scanners which plot ships in the channel between Dover and Dungeness and beside them is a huge photographic machine which records the position of shipping throughout the day, taking a photograph every minute for a period of five days before needing attention. This machinery was observed in action when a call came for a pilot to escort the ‘Aulica’ carrying methane gas extracted from the Sahara Desert.

Northern Lands

by MARY GEORGE, MBE, Director, EAW

Market Place, Helsinki

MEMORIES crowd in on me as I try to record my impressions of Finland, of the International Congress on Home Economics which I recently attended there and of the brief visit I paid to Leningrad, that most beautiful of northern cities. At the International Congress there were nearly 1000 delegates from 43 countries, including 133 from the United Kingdom. We met and were housed on the campus of the Technical University at Otaniemi, about 8 kilometres outside Helsinki and it is interesting that the Student Union of the University own and run the complex of buildings which during the long vacation become a hotel and conference centre.

Recently there has been a tremendous demand, particularly in Scandinavian countries, for the 50/50 blend of cider vinegar and unpasteurised honey, marketed by Merrydown as Honegar. This age-old mixture is strongly recommended for the relief of asthma, hayfever, arthritis and other ills and Merrydown receives many letters each year testifying to the amazing effectiveness of this product.

brief_context: Country where Honegar faced potential ban due to popularity.
brief_extract: This age-old mixture is strongly recommended for the relief of asthma, hayfever, arthritis and other ills and Merrydown receives many letters each year testifying to the amazing effectiveness of this product. So great has been the demand for Honegar in Denmark following an article in its praise in a popular magazine, that the authorities sought to have the product banned for fear of doing Danish doctors out of business! There was however such a hue and cry in the popular press that an appeal was made to the local Ombudsman, with the result that the Danes are now again allowed to import Honegar, since obviously there was no grounds for banning a product so completely free from any harmful matter.

location_standardised: North York Moors, North Yorkshire, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Where the author and his wife spent a few days.
brief_extract: Blades need sharpening, chains examined and the whole machine given a thorough overhauling. My wife and I spent a few days on the Yorkshire Moors last September just at the time when the heather (colluna vulgaris) was at its best. What a glorious sight it was—acres and acres of purple stretching away as far as the eye could see.

brief_context: One of the gardens the author visited this year.
brief_extract: It is, of course, always a great pleasure to visit these large gardens, to photograph particularly beautiful subjects or vistas and then during the long winter evenings to enjoy them all over again at your leisure and in the comfort of your own home. I have visited five this year:—Bath Botanical Gardens, notable for its interesting plants; Wakehurst in Sussex (administered by the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew); Chatsworth House, Derbyshire (noted particularly for its arboretum); Sheffield Botanical Garden, where you can see the rewarding results of making the city a smokeless zone and, finally, the Valley Gardens, Harrogate. I can recommend all of these for your visiting list next year.

I have visited five this year:—Bath Botanical Gardens, notable for its interesting plants; Wakehurst in Sussex (administered by the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew); Chatsworth House, Derbyshire (noted particularly for its arboretum); Sheffield Botanical Garden, where you can see the rewarding results of making the city a smokeless zone and, finally, the Valley Gardens, Harrogate. I can recommend all of these for your visiting list next year.

PACKMAN, Magazine Secretary, Clarkston Branch

This visit was a joint venture by members of the Clarkston and East Kilbride branches. The first objective was the reservoir which nestles in a corrie over 1,000 ft up Ben Cruachan in Argyllshire. From this reservoir water is carried down two inclined shafts to an underground power station where the electricity is generated and transmitted to the Scottish supply system via a vertical shaft.

brief_context: County where Ben Cruachan is located.

article_title: VISIT TO CRUACHAN PUMPED STORAGE POWER STATION
brief_extract: This shaft also serves as an air intake. A tailrace tunnel carries the water from the power station to Loch Awe. During the night and at week-ends, when the demand for electricity is low, water is pumped back along the same route from the Loch to the reservoir for storage.

article_title: VISIT TO THE ROYAL BRIERLEY CRYSTAL WORKS, BRIERLEY HILL
brief_extract:
VISIT TO THE ROYAL BRIERLEY CRYSTAL WORKS, BRIERLEY HILL
by MRS S. BISHOP, Magazine Secretary, Mansfield Branch

The history of this old-established works of Stevens & Williams Ltd dates back to 1610 when the Huguenot wanderers settled in the Stourbridge district because of the available fuel and fireclay, thus making the area famous for its crystal glass. Formerly known as Henzey, Tyzack and Tittery, they were recorded in parish registers as ‘Gentlemen Glass Makers’.
